findings: The study evaluated phishing awareness in a controlled experiment at an Israeli financial institution involving approximately 5000 employees and three simulated phishing emails. Personalised emails received more clicks than general emails. Click-through rates varied between business units, while the timing of training before the simulation did not significantly affect click-through rates.
evidence_from_paper: The article abstract and discussion report that employees were more likely to click simulated phishing emails using personalised phrasing. The discussion reports 1.5 to 2 times more clicks for personalised emails than general emails. Source: Hillman, Harel and Toch (2023), DOI: 10.1016/j.cose.2023.103364.
